A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ULOT research work. All 15 pages of each version, including equations, figures, Table 1, and Appendices A-C, are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 3 and Appendices B-C report original ULOT experiments on simulated SBM graphs and IBC fMRI data, including loss, runtime, label-propagation accuracy, and transported-activation results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Section 3 and Appendices B-C.

M1.justification: The FUGW training objective, parameter encoding, GCN and cross-attention architecture, node weighting, and transport-plan prediction procedure in Sections 2.1-2.3 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same simulated SBM graphs and IBC fMRI data. Graph alignment, label propagation, graph optimization, similarity analysis, and activation-transport scenarios are retained without additions or removals.

E2.justification: IBPP remains the synthetic-data comparator, and the IBC comparison retains IBPP, MM, L-BFGS-B, and entropic Sinkhorn. Naming POT in v2 identifies implementation software, not an additional evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The reported protocols remain unchanged, including 50,000 simulated training pairs, 1,000-node IBC graphs, 14,400 IBC graph pairs, the 60/20/20 split, and Table 1 settings. The POT addition discloses implementation provenance without reporting a changed procedure.

E4.justification: The parameter-path analyses, graph-optimization examples, scaling and warm-start comparisons, label-propagation accuracy surfaces, and qualitative fMRI illustration are unchanged, including the supplementary analyses in Appendices B-C.

E5.justification: Figures 7-8 retain their 20%-80% quantile reporting, and Appendix B retains the same accuracy uncertainty notation. No seed, repeated-run, confidence-interval, or significance-testing information is added or revised.

E6.justification: The numerical and qualitative results are unchanged. Examples include the 0.99 loss correlation in Figure 7, the runtime and warm-start results in Figures 7-8, and Appendix B accuracies of 0.87 +/- 0.092 and 0.74 +/- 0.11.

T1.justification: Equations 1-13, the mathematical definitions and assumptions, and the complexity arguments are retained. No mathematical derivation, theorem, or proof is added, removed, or corrected.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statement, and conclusion retain the same claims: parameter-conditioned unsupervised transport prediction, quadratic prediction complexity, competitive loss with up to 100-fold speedup, differentiability, and solver warm starts.

C2.justification: The interpretations of parameter effects, transport mass, and optimization behavior are unchanged. Section 4 retains the same precision limitations, GPU-memory constraint at graphs of at most 10,000 nodes, and future application directions.

D1.justification: Section 3.2 newly identifies POT as software used for the solver comparison. New acknowledgments identify IDRIS/GENCI computing support and credit Quang Huy Tran for FUGW solver code. Appendix A's hardware, training times, hyperparameters, and code-release statements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Flamary et al., POT: Python Optimal Transport, as reference [9], with a corresponding solver-library citation. The existing cited works and substantive positioning relative to prior research are unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds an Acknowledgments and Disclosure of Funding section and briefly expands the solver-comparison sentence. The scientific narrative and section organization otherwise remain unchanged, apart from citation renumbering and the version/date marking.

P2.justification: Added text causes limited reflow of the conclusion and bibliography on pages 9-12. Figures 1-11 and Table 1 retain their displays, captions, and placement; no scientific visual is added or redesigned.

improvement.justification: Naming POT and documenting computing, funding, and contributed solver-code support modestly improves implementation provenance and attribution transparency. The methods, empirical evidence, and limitations are unchanged, so the quality gain is confined to documentation.
